name: Shi
sweep_summary: Shi (shii1238) is not in the catalog. Two title hits.23-26, 211-236, 484-485, 498) using Polak-Bynon's data; classes it as an 'accentual' H*BH-melody system with 5 lexical schemes and states that the penult carries no pitch/length/intensity culmination, serving only as a boundary for tone rules — i.e. no word stress to code; best statement of the sweep, no catalog record to supersede. (2) Möhlig 1969 (ZDMG Suppl. I, pp.1155-1165; per Maho's note primarily on Dciriku, with Hehe, Chaga and Shi secondary): not obtained — the digitized volume exists on opendata.uni-halle.de (handles 113237-113239, OAI-PMH lists PDF + scanned bitstreams) but every page/bitstream is behind an interactive Anubis bot check, and the Wayback capture of the Teil 2 PDF is unreachable because web.archive.org refuses connections from our machine; priority medium, acquisition route recorded in. Still unobtained primary sources: Polak-Bynon 1975 A Shi Grammar (print only), Bashi Murhi-Orhakube 2012 phonology chapter (Google Books partial view but Google blocked from our machine). new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (542 pp., text layer, DDL Lyon re-typeset PDF of Philippson 1991 these d'Etat). (1) Annexe 'Resume des systemes prosodiques', PDF p. 498, entry 'Shi' under Groupe I reads exactly: '1. : oui / (2). / 3. : systeme accentuel a melodie H*BH / 4. : 5 / 5. : -cv(:)cv, -c*v(:)c`v, -c*v(:)cv, -cv(:)c*v, + 1 a prefixe marque / 6. : absente / (7) / 8. : la partie B de la melodie canonique s'associe a la more marquee / 9. : le H de droite s'associe une fois, puis le H de gauche... dissociation du dernier H devant pause s'il est associe a la more penultieme ou a la finale... / 10. : cf. 9.' The key to the numbered rubrics is on p. 497 (1 = opposition de longueur realisee, 3 = systeme tona…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No positional word stress is reported. Shi has contrastive vowel length and a tonal ('accentual' in the autosegmental sense) system: certain mores are lexically/morphologically marked (five lexical schemes for CVCV noun stems, marks on roots, object prefixes, etc.); a marked more takes the L of a canonical H-L-H melody, the left H spreads back to the beginning of the word, the right H links to one following more, and a H on the penultimate or final more delinks before pause. The position of the 'accent' is therefore lexical, not fixed, and it is realised by pitch, not by intensity or length; the penultimate carries no pitch, length or intensity culmination (unlike Nande or Nyoro-Tooro in the same survey).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress; multiple H spans arise from tone spreading, not from rhythmic stress.
new_statements.exceptions: A fifth noun scheme with a marked prefix (mostly loans, e.g. omúgozi 'corde'); some class 1a nouns and deverbatives with a long final H-toned vowel (laataa 'père'); tone associations are blocked or altered at three grades of syntactic boundary (subject/predicate, 'loose' and 'tight' liaison).
new_statements.domain_note: Philippson's 'accent'/'système accentuel' is explicitly the abstract autosegmental accent (a lexically marked more that anchors a tone melody), which he distinguishes in ch.1 from 'langues accentuelles classiques (à accent d'intensité)'. His Shi data are entirely second-hand from Polak-Bynon 1975 (grammar) and 1978 (lexicon), re-analysed; forms are word-level lexical forms plus pre-pausal (citation) realisations. Variety: Kabare (central Bushi) Shi as described by Polak-Bynon.
new_statements.identity_note: All statements concern central Shi (Mashi, JD53, glottocode shii1238, ISO shr) as spoken around Kabare (and near-identical Ngweshe), the variety described by Polak-Bynon 1975 and re-analysed by Philippson 1991; northern Karhana Shi (Havu-influenced) and the southern dialects (Kaziba, Luhwinja, Burhinyi etc.) are not covered. Not to be confused with Mashi K34 of Zambia (mash1267).

new_statements.reading: Shi has no fixed word stress: Philippson (working from Polak-Bynon's 1975 grammar) explicitly excludes Shi from the languages with pitch or length culmination on the penult and places it among languages where the penult has no phonetic prominence at all, only a role as a limit for tone rules. Word-level prominence is a lexically placed tonal accent: one marked mora per stem carrying a canonical HBH melody (five schemes for disyllabic noun stems), associated predominantly leftward. For a stress catalog this is a tonal/accentual (restricted-tone) language with no stress position to code; a first-hand statement would have to come from Polak-Bynon 1975 (A Shi Grammar, MRAC Annales 86; print only, not obtained) or Bashi Murhi-Orhakube 2012 (phonology chapter not in the open preview).

sources.note: Only front matter, introduction and ch.1 (dialects) are in the preview; the phonology chapter is not. Intro pp. 10-11 states Mashi has distinctive tone (kugéra 'passer' H vs kugera 'mesurer' L; only H marked), refers readers to Philippson 1991 for discussion of Polak-Bynon's account of the Shi tonal system, and quotes Polak-Bynon (1975: 7-8) that Cleire 1955 does not treat tone. Nothing on stress in the accessible pages.
